customize.text: Avrelian
Sacred Heir

More than six thousand years ago, in the golden kingdom of Hyperborea, people launched the "Elysium Project." They hoped to transform the world into an Elysium for humankind alone. After relentless experimentation, they mastered the power of tailoring and refining the Seeds of Life. The new humans born after such "adjustments" were supposed to wield elemental forces at will. They hoped that their descendants would produce enough food to free all life from hunger, unlock primordial secrets, and freely transform matter into energy and vice versa. When the golden kingdom was destroyed, the survivors traveled south, where they settled on Hiisi Island and became the Frostmoon Scions. The Hyperboreans left behind a supremely advanced device: the Subatomic Assembling Mass-Energy Patterning Orb, later known as the Sampo Mill. It was designed to reconstruct matter at the subatomic scale, or to transmute matter directly into stable energy. Although its structure remained largely intact, the device was unusable because the collaborative control module connected to the device was lost during the fall of Hyperborea and couldn't be replicated with existing technologies. After the discussion, it was decided to seal the device indefinitely without re-evaluating its feasibility. The SAMPO gradually transformed from a device into a religious symbol. They believed that only the heir foretold in the prophecy, who wielded the elements, could awaken the Mill and create an Elysium of eternal abundance for them. To create the ideal heir, the Frostmoon Scions continued the
of the Hyperborean era. Since the core processes, including the process of creating Fae and editing the Seeds of Life, were lost during the fall of Hyperborea, it was decided to purify the blood of the Frostmoon Scions through controlled selection. It was assumed that this would result in the birth of the prophesied Sacred Heir, who would freely command the pure, unaltered elemental forces at will, without resorting to ritual implements or sacrificing their soul, thereby achieving fusion with the world.

Several millennia later, a blessed maiden was born who, according to the prophecy, was destined to bear the sacred heir. But when the girl met a young man from the northern kingdom, she felt a love she had never felt before and abandoned her mission for the sake of the young officer. For this new feeling, this foolishness called love, she cut off her antlered crown and threw it onto the snowy ground. She wanted her unborn son, Avrelian, to live in peace and joy, never to set foot on the lands of Nod-Krai or believe in dreams of "Elysium." Though she had long since left her homeland, the new life growing within her awakened long-dormant visions of the fall of civilizations and the future of her homeland. She saw how humans first enjoyed wisdom and prosperity, followed by greed and selfish desires, each masked by noble names. From them followed hatred, curses, betrayal, strife, plunder, slaughter, and kin turning against kin. Cities were scattered across the land, some following the path of good, others the path of evil, and the divine envoys remained silent and did not interfere. But when the kings of men dared to test the
the great towers fell in flames. Like all tragic illusions, this boundless Elysium would crumble. The dying world drew near its end, and only the shadows of the past remained in its halls. But Avrelian's voice, which she had never heard before, full of compassion as soft as light, always whispered to her from the dead end of darkness and pain: <color=#ffffffd9>"I shall bring an end to the warriors of this land and raise a boundless Elysium in their place. I do this not to be king, but so that no other can ever claim that role."</color>

When spies were sent to retrieve the blessed maiden and return her to the homeland she was meant to love, the girl saw her lover's blood spilling beneath her feet and slit her throat. The Frostmoon Scions did not know that she had given birth to a son, Avrelian, and after his parents' deaths, he was adopted by a private officer named Mikhnenko, which allowed the boy to enroll in the Snezhnayan Royal Military Academy. But shortly after Avrelian was promoted to officer, he was marked as "died in the line of duty," as part of a plot hatched by Professor Rotwang of the Belyi Tsar's court and Alvis, Grand Duke of Kitezhgrad. Avrelian later returned to Nod-Krai and became the great thief Reed Miller. The professor once saw a pitch-black Elysium beyond the heavens and resolved to do everything in his power to reach it. When the Belyi Tsar sent him to Nod-Krai on a secret mission to retrieve a treasure hidden there that could upend the world, Rotwang chose to seize it not to save the world, but to use it as a means to his own ends. He believed that only those like him and Avrelian, chosen by a higher grace, were worthy of living on. It was better to find liberation by sacrificing oneself for a greater purpose than to remain lost in endless cycles of reincarnation.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Reed Miller, cast your meaningless melancholy aside, for you and I have been chosen by fate."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Come, follow me. Though the world is destined for destruction, we shall emerge from the celestial shell!"</color>

And although the professor promised Avrelian an Elysium, that world was never Avrelian’s dream. From the very beginning, Rotwang used the sacred heir only to obtain the Sampo Mill for himself. And the Elysium he spoke of was intended for him alone.

customize.text: Reed Miller

Since childhood, Avrelian had been friends with Solovei, a member of the noble Snezhnaya family whose emblem was the nightingale. Avrelian once carved the first raven emblem, imitating the nightingale, which later became the symbol of the Treasure Hoarders. As a child, Avrelian often spoke of his dream of creating an "Elysium" on earth and railed against the gods and the rich. One day, Avrelian and Solovei persuaded Governor Prokhor Trubetskoy's five-year-old adopted son, Brahe, to reveal the location of his father's treasure. They played good cop and bad cop, using both the carrot and the stick to get him to talk, and Avrelian distributed the stolen wealth to the children of Nod-Krai. But they never learned that Trubetskoy had managed to recoup three times the amount in less than three days.

<color=#ffffffd9>"It's a place my brothers and sisters remain — where they continue to endure hardships they should never have to bear. Tell me, those innocent souls — were they born to suffer like this?</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>If it's the law that is causing their suffering, then I shall rewrite the law. And if it's the corrupt nobles, then I shall purge them from their ranks!</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>One day, I'll raise an Elysium that belongs to us on this land — a land that has always belonged to us!"</color>

When Avrelian took the name Reed Miller and returned to Nod-Krai, he decided to create an "Elysium" for everyone. He gathered the outcasts and the wretched under the wings of a black raven, and thus the first Treasure Hoarders were born. At the time, they called him their leader, believing that this young man of unknown origin could break the shackles and build an equal Elysium for all who suffered. Reed Miller forged the first iron coin engraved with the raven symbol, which became the first true "Iron Coin." Later, raven seals were used to identify Treasure Hoarders and determine their status. In a world without borders, in a paradise where no one suffers from hunger or cold, the gold bestowed and governed by the Deus Auri was never meant to serve as the foundation of human cooperation. Humans should be masters of money, not its servants. Even if no one can claim the heart of gold for themselves, everyone should be able to wield the wealth that inherently belongs to everyone. Rumor had it that Reed Miller created a set of tools dubbed the "Seven Tools of the Great Thief" to destroy artificial boundaries, be they chains or state borders. The great thief was caught numerous times, but each time he escaped punishment.

<color=#ffffffd9>"To the poor, to the hungry, to the cold, to the oppressed, and the abused. To my brothers and sisters, all of you who have found your way here..."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"If you have ever suffered injustice at the hands of fate, or if you have ever wept through the night for your neighbor's pain and suffering..."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"If you, too, long for a refuge without fear, and if you, too, dream of a world where no tears are shed,"</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Then you, too, must break free of your chains and join us, your brothers and sisters."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"Let the dead bury the dead, and rise to build an Elysium for the hungry and the poor on the wealth of the high and haughty."</color>

When Reed Miller infiltrated the Frostmoon Scions to obtain the Sampo Mill, he met the twin sisters Aila and Alia, who were destined to give birth to the perfect heir. Alia, unwilling to accept such a fate, fled with Avrelian, joining the Treasure Hoarders. He swore to her never to put himself in danger or break that oath. When his friend Solovei convinced Avrelian to leave the Treasure Hoarders and go to Snezhnograd to explain himself to the Belyi Tsar, Avrelian begged Alia not to fear for him and not to shed tears for the future, for it has not yet arrived. <color=#ffffffd9>"I know you have your doubts about my friend, but please trust my plan for now. Do not worry about me, Alia. If I am indeed the prophesied Ruler of Elysium, then no fate in this world can tear me from the brethren I hold dear."</color> These were the great thief's last words to the world. In Snezhnograd, he wasn't even allowed to see the Tsar and was sent straight to the scaffold. And although Avrelian's life was over, Reed Miller's name lived on.

customize.text: Alia

When Alia fled the Frostmoon Scions with Reed Miller, they regarded her as a traitor, and her name was forgotten. After Avrelian's death, Alia donned a silver mask and claimed to be the "master thief Reed Miller who had escaped the gallows." Over the centuries, many theories have accumulated about why the great thief hid his face. Some say he did what he did to keep himself safe from the relentless searches happening in Snezhnaya, while others say that he wore a mask to hide certain marks that had been left on him by the executioner. Some tales claim the master thief put on the mask after growing weary of the love or hate of the madding crowd, and that his close shave with death had left him a changed man — taciturn and sparing with his words. Some believed the mask concealed a face as beautiful as the court Fae. No matter the truth, the master thief's silver mask has become a symbol of the great thief. Alia molded the Treasure Hoarders into a highly disciplined, quasi-military force that almost resembled a religious order. Her mantra was that no one should place their faith in gods or deities, for it was humanity alone that held the power to save its own. The Treasure Hoarders of that era could be described as "an irreligious religious order." Under the name "Reed Miller," she gathered a large group of bandits, and together, they picked the governor's palace in Nod-Krai clean in a single night. All the countless curios, antiques, Mora, and jewels that they made off with were given by Alia to the poor of Nasha Town. Although the Treasure Hoarders had distanced themselves from Avrelian's dream of Elysium, and for the people, those ideals and Elysium were as distant as the moon in the sky, the great thief Reed Miller began to be revered in Nod-Krai. Perhaps they dreamed of someone like Alia, who could scatter riches directly into their hands, without any effort on their part.

<color=#ffffffd9>"Laugh at their fearful lies, brethren. For they cannot kill Reed Miller, the master thief."</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>"They have but murdered a single crow, but with tomorrow's light, a murder of crows shall rise to be at my back."</color>

After Avrelian's death, when Alia became the new Reed Miller, Solovei arrived in Nod-Krai and began to interfere with Professor Rotwang's plans. Although Alia distrusted Solovei, she knew that using the Sampo Mill would pose great danger, so she pretended to be his close friend to gain his trust and set off with him. When Professor Rotwang built a heaven-reaching tower in Nod-Krai, named the Pillar of Embla, he intended to use the Sampo Mill to siphon the land's power and, through that tower, ascend to the "Elysium" he believed lay beyond the sky. Had his scheme succeeded, all of Nod-Krai — its soil and every living being upon it — would have become fuel for his ascent. Alia and Solovei did everything they could to stop him, but at the time, they were too weak. When they reached the Pillar of Embla, Rotwang was one step away from his goal. Realizing there was no other choice, Alia cast herself into the Sampo Mill and, with her own body, ignited it with the purified blood of the Frostmoon Scions. Alia's sacrifice thwarted the Professor's plans and destroyed him for the first time.

customize.text: Brahe

Brahe was the adopted son of the Fae Lord Prokhor Trubetskoy, ruler of all of Nod-Krai. Some claimed he was actually the governor's illegitimate son, and because he had Fae blood in his veins, he was more handsome than most humans. Like Avrelian, he attended the Military Academy, though he enrolled long after Avrelian had graduated. After graduating, Brahe returned to Nod-Krai, where, like all the other nobles of Snezhnaya at the time, he indulged in a life of excess and pleasure. This continued until one night, when he saw Alia robbing the governor's palace and fell in love with her at first sight. He was so captivated by her that he even abandoned his noble life to join the Treasure Hoarders. Brahe inherited the Grand Duke title from his adoptive father, but when Solovei the Torchforger asked the Tsaritsa to grant the borderlands autonomy, Grand Duke Brahe also appeared before the throne. There, he willingly gave up any claim to the land and all it held. He then entrusted the governor's palace to the Lightkeepers, who turned it into a military fortress. After the death of his beloved, Brahe adopted the name Reed Miller and continued robbing the rich to help the poor and the people of Nod-Krai. Brahe believed that it was impossible to force a person who had never known kindness, who had suffered humiliation all his life, to believe that he should love his neighbor and his enemy. What he saw robbed him of his idealistic faith in human nature and the dream of an Elysium for all.

After Professor Rotwang's death, he was left with followers who faithfully continued to serve the professor. One of these followers was Inspector R. M. Morozov, who built a bunker to protect against the apocalypse on Wavechaser Plain. Although Morozov claimed the bunker served as protection from the forces of the Abyss, he was actually awaiting Rotwang's return and conducting experiments specifically for this purpose. Families with children gathered in the shelter, all believing the world outside had been destroyed by the apocalypse, preventing them from leaving. Under Morozov's orders, Senior Researcher Grazyna Myklukho conducted experiments with kuuvahki, as some studies indicated that prior to the apocalypse, kuuvahki exerted a catalytic effect on the growth of certain plants, inducing developmental mutations that result in phenotypes more attuned to kuuvahki. By artificial regulation of the mutation process, Grazyna was able to develop special plants, which Brahe, who had infiltrated the bunker, later named Mandragora. Grazyna submitted a request to upgrade the existing ventilation system by installing a pipeline to carry kuuvahki, circulated by the plants, and Morozov agreed. Grazyna didn't suspect that this system could be used not only for kuuvahki but also to amplify Abyssal pollution, creating the illusion of a destroyed world. The researcher hoped that one day, people would emerge to the surface and find a new world, and that her plants would help them rid themselves of the black filth. Gradually, due to the Abyssal leak and the escaped Abyssal monsters, people began to die. Grazyna asked Morozov to immediately cease all further testing of the purification system and destroy all living specimens from the Abyss, but he refused. Senior Mechanic Kotelnikov discovered Morozov's true motives and passed the information on to Grazyna so she could save the children. Furthermore, Brahe left her a message that if she wished to leave the bunker, she was to hand over an item to any of the Treasure Hoarders, and they would lead her to the great thief Reed Miller. When the researcher learned of what was happening, she asked Brahe to secretly remove the children from the facility. He said he knew an eccentric old hunter, probably Sukhotin, who was an old acquaintance of the Frostmoon Scions' Moonchanter. Together with Brahe, Grazyna managed to destroy Morozov and seal the bunker, but Brahe warned her that the Abyssal contamination in these parts could not be eradicated overnight, and that Morozov would one day rise as a mad monster, only to be destroyed by the hero of the prophecy of the Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions. Until then, he would forever wander these Abyss-corroded ruins, devouring the flesh and blood of those who stray in here. As Brahe had predicted, Morozov returned as the Ultimate Calamity, believing the world to be destroyed, having broken free of the heavenly shell and no longer bound by gravity or the laws of fate. The Ultimate Calamity was destroyed by the Traveler and Paimon, who had entered the bunker.

Ten years after Alia's sacrifice, the Treasure Hoarders had scattered across the globe, justifying their atrocities against the innocent with the words of Reed Miller. Whether it's wandering merchants barely scraping by, or overworked laborers starving for their next meal, anyone could be branded a "lackey of princes" or a "traitor who betrays his brothers and neighbors," and therefore "ripe for their noble robbery." Those who came before overcame evil with noble ideals, but now, the bandits waved the same banner, declaring that anyone who opposes them is an enemy of those noble ideals, thus embodying the very evil that was once defeated. And though Brahe fought the bandits who committed evil in Reed Miller's name, oppressing the laboring poor by sending them to the Eye of Kratti to sleep with the fishes for good, he feared what would become of the Treasure Hoarders after his death. No one could guarantee that their once-noble ideals wouldn't be distorted beyond recognition, that crimes he couldn't even imagine wouldn't be committed under their guise. Brahe couldn't place all his hopes on human nature, for humans breed evil as naturally as bees produce honey. He didn't want Reed Miller's name to fade into the stream of history and be forgotten, or for that name and the ideals it once represented to be distorted by villains in future generations and cursed by humanity. So he decided to bury so-called ideals in history, smothering them with countless contradictory, absurd, laughable yet irresistible stories, until every trace of meaning is worn away and only a sweeping legend remains. This way, anyone who commits evil in our name will never be mistaken for a serious idealist, but rather a childish dreamer lost in their romantic tales. And as long as the legends of the Great Treasure live, gamblers dreaming of making a fortune overnight will repeat the name of the "Master Thief Reed Miller" again and again. If the rebels of the future truly needed a new banner, they would find their hero, and his name may be anything but "Master Thief Reed Miller." After Brahe, many tried to call themselves Reed Miller, but no one else's name has survived into history.

customize.text: Proof of the Cognoscenti

Brahe converted his father's hidden hiding place into a treasury, where he transferred iron coins using weasels, which he dubbed "Weasel Thieves" and recruited as members of the Treasure Hoarders. But just three weeks after its completion, the treasury was discovered by Dmitri Dubrovich Sukhotin, trusted aide of the Grand Duke Filipov, a third-class military officer, and Chief Instructor of the Snezhnayan Royal Military Academy. According to the official version, Sukhotin died during the Cataclysm in battle alongside His Majesty the Tsar, sacrificing himself for the nation. In reality, he renounced his noble title and name to devote the rest of his life to protecting children on the border, the homeless children who roam the wastelands. Brahe's chosen location seemed suspicious to him, and he assumed it was a slaver's camp, so he burst in with the intention of dealing with the bandits. Although he didn't recognize Brahe, he remembered his father's name. After listening to Brahe's explanation of the treasure vault, the old man fell silent for a moment, then said that if a student had proposed such a ridiculous scheme back when he was Chief Instructor, he would've thrown it straight back and ordered them to start over. Realizing that if anyone were to break in again using their sharp instincts, the plan would be pointless, Brahe decided to make it impossible for people to discover the place. He decided to turn the story of the Master Thief Reed Miller into the "Proof of the Cognoscenti," since knowing the key's existence would prevent people from seeking other ways to open the door. He then spread several stories about treasure hunters who had tried shortcuts but had failed, disseminating them under the names of "Brahe the Bard" and "Grand Duke Trubetskoy." This was enough to firmly convince future generations of the necessity of searching for the Proofs of the Cognoscenti, which would lead to the Great Treasure hidden east of the moon, west of the sun.

Five Proofs of the Cognoscenti were created and hidden: a flower, a feather, a watch, a goblet, and a mask. The flower, Memorata-Cognoscenti's Jest, was kept by Brahe's descendant, Hiljetta. She considered her ancestor unworthy of the name Reed Miller and was a staunch supporter of Reed Miller's dream, though no one knew what he truly dreamed of. Hiljetta gave the Proof of the Cognoscenti to the Traveler and Paimon after they collected the remaining artifacts and promised to continue Avrelian's dream. The Inscripta-Cognoscenti's Feather was hidden amidst a shipwreck near the Eye of Kratti. A whirlpool had once existed there, destroying countless ships, and many who sought the Proof of the Cognoscenti perished in pursuit. The watch, Devocina-Cognoscenti's Sorrow, was hidden in an apocalypse bunker Brahe had once infiltrated. The Traveler and Paimon discovered it after killing Morozov for good and cleansing the bunker from the Abyss. The goblet, Weavenexa-Cognoscenti's Intoxication, changed hands many times until it was obtained by Poruchik Raskolnikov of the Fatui to deliver to Snezhnograd. Netochka, the daughter of a police captain who knew Raskolnikov, went to the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau to retrieve the Proof of the Cognoscenti, with the help of the Traveler and Paimon. As a result, the girl deemed them more worthy successors to the great thief and gave the goblet to them. The last Proof of the Cognoscenti, Stratagema-Cognoscenti's Mask, was kept for a long time by the good-natured mechanic, Papa Wrench. When Papa Wrench died of illness, his friend Tolfin, Hiljetta's grandson and Brahe's heir, began telling stories about the Proof of the Cognoscenti, thus attracting the attention of the Traveler and Paimon.

When the Traveler and Paimon collected all five Proofs of the Cognoscenti, they were able to open the Treasure Hoarders' vault, sealed by the statue of a Weasel Thief. But instead of treasure, they discovered only a pile of iron coins, the kind in circulation at the time, a sunken ship, and Brahe's notes, where he asked the followers to keep the legend of the great thief. Perhaps five hundred years ago, there had been a secret haven for the Treasure Hoarders, but the landscape had changed over the years, and the ship of their dreams, having run aground, was never able to set sail. The most important treasure was the raven's mark, carved by Avrelian as a child. Thus, the Great Treasure, hidden east of the moon, west of the sun, was recovered five hundred years later.

customize.text: Legends

When Brahe decided to clothe Reed Miller's name and his ideals in legend, people spun countless legends caught betwixt truth and falsehood, their greatest anecdotes always laced with lies. From lovers' whispered pillow talk to drunkards' agitated shouts, the tales of the thief extraordinaire enchanted all who heard them. Thus the legend grew, until the singer and the hero of the songs merged into a single riddle, passed down from poet to poet over long, indistinguishable nights. Some said that Reed Miller was sentenced to death more than once, but each time he managed to escape at the last moment with the help of friends and his instruments. In some versions of the story, several of his followers voluntarily accepted death in the place of their revered Lord of Elysium. Some believed that the first Frostmoon Scions' Moonchanter, Aila, once convinced Reed Miller to steal the
which had bewitched the Archpriestess. Some believed that Aila, who never truly forgave Avrelian for her sister's escape, fell in love with the great thief and therefore remained unmarried for the rest of her life. There is also a legend about a pebble, the hole in which was believed to be a shelter revealed to the Fae by the Frost Moon and a gateway to the afterlife. In a story popular in Nasha Town, the legendary thief, Reed Miller, was surrounded when a runestone given to him by a holy lady of the Frost Moon as a token of her love allowed him to conceal himself and escape his pursuers. Some said that he outwitted the most elite guards in the northern realm with a fake medallion and emptied the governor's palace, and later, disguised as a special envoy of the Tsar on a secret inspection, he squeezed the entire treasury out of Viscount Schpekin for his hospitality. In the popular comedy "A Family of Noblemen: The Gentlemen Porfiry" staged by the Korolevskiy Troupe, the master thief, in one of his fleeting appearances, posed before the nobles as a holy fool who could hear the spirits. He listened to their confessions, composing a new verse of a ballad from each shameful secret, which bards sang in taverns and on the streets to the laughter and jeers of the common folk.
Several legends about Reed Miller are connected with the governor of Nod-Krai, the Fae Prokhor Trubetskoy. In one of them, the governor had an adopted human daughter, young Leonita Prokhorovna Trubetskaya, and to celebrate her coming of age, her father decided to throw a grand ball to find her a groom. As a gift, Trubetskoy presented his daughter with a necklace from Fontaine, containing a precious stone that outshone even the finest stones of Natlan. A jeweler from Fontaine arrived with her lover at the governor's castle with this necklace, and together they escorted Reed Miller, disguised as a footman, into the palace. On the front page of the morning newspaper, Leonita saw a letter adorned with black feathers.

<color=#ffffffd9>Dear Lord Trubetskoy,</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Three nights from now, on the dark night of the new moon, your treasure will be mine.</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>I thank you for your kind generosity. With the greatest regard,</color>
<color=#ffffffd9>Reed Miller.</color>

The newspaper containing Miller's letter quickly flew off the shelves, and for the next few days, all of Nod-Krai was abuzz with anticipation of the inevitable showdown between the great thief and Governor Trubetskoy. The governor's palace was put on high alert, and every guest was subjected to a thorough search. When guests saw Leonita, they whispered why the noble Fae would need to adopt a human. The answer lay in Leonita's origins, which also answered the question of the lord's source of such wealth. Leonita was an orphan of the Frostmoon Scions, capable of activating the Sampo Mill, a magical relic that brought untold riches, which Trubetskoy had acquired. From the very beginning of the ball, Leonita noticed that the people around her seemed shrouded in a silvery haze, and with each passing second, the haze grew brighter. At times, a silvery glow also flowed over her own body. Her father said it was an illness that needed constant treatment, a flaw inherent in her human nature. Suddenly, a precious stone from her necklace fell to the floor, her heart began to beat in time with a silvery pulse, and an unknown force prevented her legs from moving. A young man approached her, saying that Leonita's father had ordered her taken away, but she recognized him as Reed Miller. But although the lord had set a trap to prevent the "greatest treasure" from being stolen, for Reed Miller, that treasure wasn't the Sampo Mill, but Leonita herself. And then the girl realized that she was the true source of the governor's wealth, and the "procedures" were not for healing at all, but rituals necessary to ensure Sampo Mill produced a continuous flow of diamonds. Though part of her has always known, she has never allowed herself to face the truth until now. After this, Reed Miller made off with every governor's treasure, and Leonita, who had fallen in love with him from the moment she saw his true face, forsake her gilded cage to wander the world with the great thief.
One of the legends about Reed Miller and Prokhor Trubetskoy also tells of the great thief's partner, the beautiful Wagtail, or "A" to the select few. There was no other woman like her in all of Nod-Krai: a femme fatale who could outshine Reed Miller himself with her fame and mastery of theft. She could easily acquire any treasure, even the most valuable, if she so desired, but the only treasure that had so far eluded Wagtail was Reed Miller's heart. Perhaps this is why she so obsessively desired this handsome and mysterious man, willing to do anything to win his heart. One day, Reed Miller decided to steal the Sampo Mill and the rest of the stolen treasures from the governor, but Wagtail promised to reach the Mill before him. When Reed Miller managed to get there before his partner, the governor summoned detectives from Snezhnaya, who suddenly burst into the palace and shackled him. It turned out that the detectives were the great thief and Wagtail, who deceived the Oprichniki. To Reed Miller, the governor's treasures had been stolen from the destitute who lived there, so there was no difference between a bandit who robbed people and a governor who oppressed them. The Treasure Hoarders defended freedom the only way they could, because no one else would fight for it, but none of the treasures ended up in their pockets, and each one had to be returned to its rightful owner. When Wagtail heard this, she sighed quietly: "Oh dear, this man truly is beyond help. He speaks of laying no claim to treasure, when he holds the Frost Moon's most prized gem in his hand..." Hearing her words, the governor's adopted daughter, Shadow Weasel, was stunned and looked away from her father, who sat bound in the center of the hall. <color=#ffffffd9>"Wh—When? Mr. Reed Miller should've given the Sampo Mill to that holy woman. Wait. He didn't secretly swap it for a fake while we weren't looking, did he...?" "Ah, you don't get it, do you? That's exactly how he deceived you young ladies."</color> The woman sighed dramatically. <color=#ffffffd9>"What he has stolen for himself is the heart of the Frost Moon's daughter."</color>
Another legend about a great thief and a governor tells how the governor's advisers worked day and night, desperately struggling to find new and exotic clothes for their master, until one day a young tailor dressed in black appeared at the palace. He claimed to have inherited the mysterious techniques of the golden realm and that he could spin crystals that glow like the silver moon into thread for weaving clothes. The governor was overjoyed and promised to reward the young tailor generously if he stayed at the palace and made him clothes. The young tailor asked the governor to deliver a vast quantity of Moonfall Silver to his workshop and demanded that no one disturb him while he worked. When the scheduled time arrived, the governor found the workshop completely empty, with neither Moonfall Silver nor any clothing to be seen. The governor, eagerly awaiting the opportunity to try on his new suit, anxiously asked where all the Moonfall Silver had gone and where the promised moonlight suit was. The tailor raised his hands as if holding fabric, shook it, and said, <color=#ffffffd9>"See? I took the Moonfall Silver you sent me and wove it into this gown, as pure as moonlight itself — too pure, in fact, for a fool or an unremarkable man to even perceive."</color> The governor saw nothing, but he refused to admit he was a fool or that he was in the wrong place, so, following the tailor's instructions, he "put on" the "moonlight gown." To show off his extraordinary new gown, the governor decided to parade it and himself along the busiest street in town, but suddenly, in the midst of the parade, a child with a shell on his belt shouted out, <color=#ffffffd9>"The governor isn't wearing any clothes!"</color> The tailor was none other than Reed Miller in disguise. He exchanged all the Moonfall Silver the governor had sent him for Mora and distributed it to the poor townsfolk. When the governor held a parade, Reed Miller watched from a rooftop.

Another legend tells of a great thief and a man named Zima, originally from Snezhnaya. He was born in a small town southeast of Snezhnograd, where villagers harvested ice beneath the snow-capped mountain peaks. On snowy nights, they told one another stories. They said that some Snegurochka were looking for love, which warms mere mortals in the cold wind, but when they were betrayed, they turned their lovers into frozen statues. Zima's companion, having fallen in love with such a Snegurochka, froze to death on the side of a mountain, and even after death, a crazy smile remained on his face. Zima found it a monotonous way to die. He was drawn to adventure, and he wanted to find his destiny, unlike others, so he went south to the archipelago in the middle of the blue sea, where he first heard about Reed Miller. At that time, there were rumors that he had been captured by the governor and taken to Snezhnograd for a hanging on the public square, but just as everyone believed his story would end with a swaying corpse, the governor's vault was found emptied with a taunting message etched in gold dust on the wall. No one knew how the great thief managed to escape the noose, but his miraculous return turned him into a tavern legend and an idol to the youth. So when the master thief reappears, buys a three-masted ship, and starts recruiting sailors seeking adventure and fortune at the harbor, Zima offers his name without a second thought. Although Miller became famous for robbing the rich and giving the loot to the poor, he walked along the sea as carefully as if he were a spice merchant and not a great thief. He spent days skirting around those regions, avoiding the dark abysses where dangerous creatures lurk as well as the serpent-infested Sea of Mist. Life on the ship consisted of scrubbing decks, patching sails, and scurvy gums. To Zima, it all felt too safe, familiar, and dull. At night, he prayed to the inky sea for a real storm, or for some monstrous kraken to rise from the depths. His prayers were answered, and one day a song was heard in the azure waters. It was not a human song, and it had no melody, but it instantly ensnared the souls of the sailors. From the water emerged the pale, hauntingly beautiful face of a siren, who demanded a sacrifice or the ship would be sunk. But Reed Miller refused to make the sacrifice and instead ordered the entire crew to plug their ears with beeswax so as not to hear the siren's haunting song. Seized by panic and the deadly song, the sailors hurled the crates of Mora looted from the governor's palace overboard, thinking the gold might serve as payment. But the siren did not even look at the gold coins plunging into the water, because human wealth meant nothing to her. Her greedy gaze was focused on the sailors themselves. The master thief had no choice but to choose a victim, and he put his cold blade to Zima's throat, but Zima didn't even resist. This was the moment he had traveled so far for. As the icy waters rise above his head, the face of his long-lost friend appears before him, frozen in sculpture, still wearing that faint, familiar, ecstatic smile sealed by the snow maiden's kiss. All his life, Zima has abhorred following a pattern, running from every known ending, only to realize in this final moment that every escape has been a flight into another mirror. Some versions of the tales about Reed Miller, the legendary thief, even tell of a so-called "King of Whales" who helped Reed and his merry companions resist the sirens' bewitching song — and, in turn, caused the siren queen herself to fall in love with him at first sight.
There's a legend about Reed Miller and the Platinum Piece. Viscount Andrei Dmitriyevich Shuisky once fell in love with Miss Milady de Este, a celebrated Fontainian diva from the Opera Epiclese. Resentful of his vain wife, the viscount decided to get rid of her. He then appropriated the treasures given to him for safekeeping by Grand Duke Brahe Prokhorovich Trubetskoy, including the platinum piece, and accused his wife of theft. When "Brahe" exposed the viscount, the latter tried to justify himself by accusing the Grand Duke of slander, but Trubetskoy then asked Shuisky to remove the glove from his right hand, where he had hidden the platinum piece in the place of the cut-off finger. Later, the police arrived at Trubetskoy's mansion and encountered the real Grand Duke Brahe. The police chief recounted how "Brahe" had first arrived as Her Majesty's special envoy, how he had instantly seen through Viscount Shuisky's ruses, confronted him, and knocked him unconscious with a single punch before the man could even draw his pistol. He also recounted how the Grand Duke had personally recovered the stolen platinum piece, and in an act of great mercy helped the locals bury the unfortunate Viscountess. The police chief said that the criminal, attempting to cover his tracks, had planted the body of some poor soul to deceive the police into thinking an even more horrific series of murders was behind the crime. Upon hearing of the incident, the real Grand Duke smashed a cup in anger, as the police had been tricked by the Great Thief Reed Miller. He assumed Brahe's appearance and took his name, so he could enter Shuisky's mansion unhindered and steal the priceless platinum piece as easily as one might fish for Mora out of a pocket. This was not the first time Grand Duke Brahe Trubetskoy had encountered the Great Thief. Before, he had already been played all too often by Miller's beautiful female companion, one who named herself "Wagtail." Even the very mention of Miller's name was enough to give him a headache. He realized that he had once again become the laughingstock of Snezhnaya and had been outwitted by the Great Thief.

customize.name: Devocina-Cognoscenti's Sorrow
customize.desc: A timepiece long since stopped. It is said to be a keepsake from Reed Miller, the founder of the Treasure Hoarders.

customize.name: Treasure Hoarder Insignia
customize.desc: A signet that proudly represents its owner's position as member of the Treasure Hoarders. The pursuit of treasure knows no bounds. That said... Is being a thief something to be proud of?

customize.name: Silver Raven Insignia
customize.desc: A raven insignia used by members of the Treasure Hoarders to identify each other. The Treasure Hoarders ask for no resume. Anyone who has an insatiable desire for treasure and is backed up by an equal amount of courage can become a worthy member.

customize.name: Golden Raven Insignia
customize.desc: A raven insignia that symbolizes the pride and the guiding principle of the Treasure Hoarders. Whether it's hidden amidst the vastness of the land or in the depths of the seas, as long as there are treasures to be hunted down, the spirit of Treasure Hoarders, who will stop at nothing to acquire them, will never die.

customize.name: Teachings of Elysium
customize.desc:
Talent Level-Up material.
"Elysium" is the dream of the land beneath the moon.
There are those who are desperate to get in, and those who are desperate to get out. Perhaps Elysium is not a place one can ever truly reach.

customize.name: Guide to Elysium
customize.desc:
Talent Level-Up material.
"Elysium" is the dream of the land beneath the moon.
To create a paradise without borders or distinctions upon a land overflowing with bitterness and sorrow — though it might be but a childish delusion, it may yet be a foundation for the future.

customize.name: Philosophies of Elysium
customize.desc:
Talent Level-Up material.
"Elysium" is the dream of the land beneath the moon.
Seldom do we share the same dreams of paradise. For those who wish not to settle for the present, there is no greater paradise than Nod-Krai. Yet for all the rest, the truth is quite the opposite.

customize.name: Artful Device Fragment
customize.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
An intricate device once known as the "Seven Tools of the Great Thief." Rumors claim it was created by the legendary thief, Reed Miller.
Just as the first Treasure Hoarders came from all walks of life, this combination of tools meant for different purposes was designed to break down artificial boundaries, regardless of whether they were chains or borders.
It should be noted that there are more than seven tools, its just that people are accustomed to using seven to describe anything numerous. Perhaps it is for the same reason that the world is believed to have only seven forms of order.

customize.name: Artful Device Replica
customize.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
Just as the legendary thief's tools have been imitated by countless others, so has his name.
In a sense, it was not the people who thirsted for something more who stole Reed Miller's name, but rather Reed Miller who stole the identity that was originally theirs alone. These viewpoints are just two sides of the same coin.

customize.name: Artful Device Inheritance
customize.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
Word on the street is that the legendary thief, Reed Miller, has been sentenced to death several times, yet he's always managed to escape at the last minute with the help of his friends — and his tools.
In some versions of these stories, several of his followers willingly died in his place for their revered King of Elysium. Naturally, these versions can't compete with the more popular drunken stories full of romance and bliss. Since there has never been a shackle that could restrain the legendary thief, it is only natural to assume that no ending could do the same.

customize.name: Artful Device Wish
customize.desc:
Weapon Ascension Material.
"The poor, the starving, the wretched, the oppressed! My exiled brothers and sisters!"
"If you, too, have tasted indignities at the cruel hands of fate! If you, too, have wept in the night at the plight of your neighbors!"
"If you, too, have longed for a shelter from fear! If you, too, have dreamed of a world where no tears are shed!"
"Then join us, your brothers and sisters, in breaking the chains of slavery!"
"Let the dead bury the dead, for you will rise up, and with the treasures of the haughty, we will build an Elysium without boundaries!"
